summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with a history of endometriosis and bipolar disorder was admitted for acute left lower quadrant abdominal pain and nausea, consistent with a flare of chronic endometriosis. Imaging showed no acute surgical pathology, and she was started on Depo-Provera for symptom management. During the hospitalization, she developed a low-grade fever, and a chest X-ray revealed right lower lobe pneumonia, likely healthcare-associated. She was treated with IV antibiotics via a PICC line, later transitioned to oral levofloxacin. Her pain and respiratory symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with follow-up arranged and instructions to avoid QT-prolonging medications during antibiotic treatment.
